card: This pull request updates Tapscript Miniscript duplicate-key checks to compare public keys as 32-byte x-only keys rather than 33-byte compressed keys. Previously, tr() descriptors containing keys that differed only in parity byte passed sanity checks even though both branches serialize to identical scripts on-chain, violating BIP-379 and enabling third-party transaction malleation. The change also adds an option to skip Miniscript sanity checks when deserializing or exporting existing wallet records, preventing loadwallet failures on wallets that already hold non-sane descriptors. P2WSH descriptors continue to distinguish 33-byte compressed keys.
changed_since_previous: Added a commit introducing a require_sane flag (defaulting to true) to Parse() and ParseScript(), allowing wallet descriptor loading and watch-only export to bypass Miniscript sanity checks so existing wallets with legacy non-sane descriptors continue to load.
evidence: PR description: "Because a single signature satisfies both branches, third parties could malleate transactions by altering branch selectors without holding private keys, violating BIP-379 non-malleability invariants."

Commit 4e549915cc: "Existing wallets created before enforcing Tapscript x-only duplicate-key checks may store descriptors such as tr(K,or_i(pk(02X),pk(03X))) that now fail IsSane(), causing loadwallet to fail with error -4."
Linked issue #36414: "descriptor: tr() duplicate-key check misses keys that differ only in parity"
problem: Tapscript serializes public keys without parity on-chain, but Miniscript duplicate-key checks compared 33-byte CPubKeys. Descriptors with keys differing only in parity prefix (such as pk(02X) and pk(03X)) passed sanity checks despite serializing to identical script instructions, violating BIP-379 and allowing third parties to malleate transactions by switching execution branches. Enforcing this check without adjusting wallet loading would also cause loadwallet to fail for existing wallets that already contain such descriptors.

risk.why: A mistake in descriptor parsing or sanity bypass logic could prevent existing wallets from loading or allow invalid descriptors into the wallet.

summary: Compares public keys as 32-byte x-only public keys rather than 33-byte compressed keys during Tapscript Miniscript duplicate-key checks, rejecting descriptors with keys differing only in parity. In addition, it adds a require_sane parameter to descriptor parsing so existing wallets with previously stored descriptors that fail Miniscript sanity checks can still be loaded and exported. Segwit v0 (P2WSH) descriptors continue to distinguish 33-byte compressed keys.
